answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it can submit jobs or earn reputation. If rewards depend on completed work verified by independent counterparties, spinning up a thousand accounts does not create a thousand units of influence: each account needs its own locked stake, and dishonest work risks slashing it. The attacker pays an orchard-sized capital cost and gives up liquidity; naming agents sonnet or lotus changes nothing. The mechanism raises the price of Sybil influence, though it cannot prevent a wealthy attacker from buying it.
